summary: Isaiah 11 (16 verses) continues the story of holiness. Starting with 'A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.', it moves through themes of holiness, judgment and calls readers toward hope.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows holiness lived out in assyrian crisis, exile hope. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.
They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea.
There will be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.

questions.question: What is happening in Isaiah 11?
questions.answer: In 16 verses, this chapter isaiah 11 (16 verses) continues the story of holiness. starting with 'a shoot will come out of the stock of jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.', it moves through themes of holiness, judgment and calls readers toward hope. The setting is assyrian crisis, exile hope, written to judah. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Isaiah and why 11 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally isaiah son of amoz, addressed to judah around ~700 bc. This chapter fits the book's purpose as prophecy — its themes of holiness, judgment build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'righteousness' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Being in right standing, doing what is right. In this chapter, it appears in context of holiness. For a first-time reader: think of it as being in right standing, doing what is right, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through holiness and judgment, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 11 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about holiness. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?

glossary.def: Being in right standing, doing what is right
